refusalBeforeMutation.how: every case declares its exact permitted push count; precondition refusals declare zero, the accepted branch declares one, and the post-attempt failures declare exactly one attempted push followed by the failure
refusalBeforeMutation.negativeControl: a deliberately bad wrapper that pushes and only then reports the expected refusal is run through the same assertions and must be rejected, which is what stops the zero-push check passing vacuously

selfTestSwitch.behaviour: runs only the harness-negative control, which the full run also always includes; the switch makes it separately addressable rather than optional

observations.detail: Previously a branch differing only in letter case was accepted and pushed. The hardened harness demonstrated it, and the -cnotcontains edit closed it. Two cases now pin the refusal.

If git emitted no line at all for branch --show-current the wrapper would fail on a null method call instead of its detached-HEAD message. Real git prints an empty line, which reaches the intended refusal. It refuses either way.

reviewedNewBaseline.conclusion: The current script is adopted as the reviewed new baseline. This accepts the loss of exact prior byte reconstruction and certifies present behaviour only; it does not certify historical equivalence and does not relax any push rule.
futureEditProtocol: prove that removing the inserted byte span reproduces the pre-edit hash

caseSensitiveBranchHardening.authority: owner order of 2026-10-16 section 2B, a narrow containment hardening
caseSensitiveBranchHardening.why: Git refs differing only in case can be distinct refs, so a differently cased spelling is not the authorized ref. The previous comparison used PowerShell -notcontains, which is case-insensitive, and the hardened harness demonstrated the wrapper accepting and pushing a case variant before the change.
caseSensitiveBranchHardening.change: one comparison operator: -notcontains became -cnotcontains on the branch check
caseSensitiveBranchHardening.scope: branch membership only. The origin, qualified-baseline ancestry, repository-root and destructive-operation restrictions are untouched, and the Windows path comparisons remain case-insensitive because file paths are not Git refs.

escalatedDecision.question: Does Brachiosaurus get three roots on Summon Nature's Ally VII only, as the order states, or six roots across both Summon Monster VII and Nature's Ally VII, as the printed table and the project roster catalog indicate?
escalatedDecision.orderText: Brachiosaurus is new: SNA VII only, three roots (VII one, VIII 1d3, IX 1d4+1), no Monster row and no celestial/fiendish execution children.
conflictingEvidence: The Summon Monster VII 7th-level list prints "Brachiosaurus (dinosaur)*" alongside Dire crocodile*, Dire shark*, Giant squid*, Mastodon (elephant)*, Roc* and Tyrannosaurus (dinosaur)*.

src/KingmakerGunslinger/Summoning/ExpandedSummoningIdealRosterCatalog.cs records R("brachiosaurus","Brachiosaurus",7,7,25,...) - monster tier 7 AND nature's ally tier 7 - in the same two-tier shape that gives Summon-Monster-only outsiders such as Vrock and Xill a null nature's ally tier.
Sprint 24's Tyrannosaurus, also recorded 7 / 7, was published on both lists.
escalatedDecision.whyBlockingForThisPart: Identities are allocated once and append-only, and the root structure determines the identity allocation, the execution children, the published surface counts and the native route census. Implementing the wrong one cannot be cleanly withdrawn.
workProceedingMeanwhile: the frozen source contract and both recorded resolutions

escalatedDecision.decisionText: Brachiosaurus gets three roots on Summon Nature's Ally only - VII one, VIII 1d3, IX 1d4+1 - with no Summon Monster row and no celestial/fiendish execution children.
escalatedDecision.decisionRationaleRecorded: The order was followed as written. Because identities are allocated once and append-only, this is the reversible direction: adding the Summon Monster VII rows in a later sprint is purely additive, whereas publishing Monster rows the owner did not want could not be cleanly withdrawn. The source discrepancy is preserved in this ledger rather than discarded, so a later sprint can act on it without re-deriving it.

openBlocker.what: Section 13 requires original project-authored geometry and painting. The icon catalog derives from the creature catalog, so registering Brachiosaurus makes it want a hundred-and-twentieth entry, and that entry needs an original 128x128 RGBA creature painting plus its source painting, both hashed, exactly like the 119 that exist.
openBlocker.whatCanBeAuthoredHere: The mesh JSON is deterministic structured geometry of the kind Sprint 24 shipped and can be authored programmatically.
openBlocker.whatCannotBeAuthoredHere: The 128x128 icon and the 512x512 albedo are paintings. The 119 existing icons were produced with image generation or Blender renders, and no such capability is available in this session. Nothing was substituted, approximated or procedurally faked.
openBlocker.whyLeftFailing: They are the honest signal that the art is outstanding. Moving the 119 pin or inventing a placeholder PNG would turn a real gap into a green gate.
